name: claude-monkey-bar
description: ✼ 67% · Claude session and weekly usage limits real-time on the VS Code status bar

claudeUsage.updateInterval.description: Update interval in seconds (default: 300 = 5 minutes). Values below 30 are treated as 30. The usage endpoint refuses requests that come too often, so short intervals can leave the data older than a long one would.

claudeUsage.showNotifications.description: Show a notification when a limit passes 90%. Each limit is announced once per reset period.

enumDescriptions: The highest of all limits that can raise a warning
Your own layout, written in the Custom Format section below
claudeUsage.statusBarDisplay.description: What to display in the status bar.

claudeUsage.statusBarFormat.markdownDescription:
Layout of the status bar, used only while **What to display** is set to `custom`.

A name in braces inserts that limit's utilization as a whole number:

- `{5h}` session, `{7d}` weekly
- `{opus}` `{sonnet}` `{cowork}` `{apps}` those weekly limits
- `{haiku}` `{sonnet}` `{opus}` `{fable}` `{mythos}` a weekly limit that applies to one model only
- `{max}` the highest limit that can raise a warning

Anything else is written out as typed, so `%`, separators and [product icons](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/icons-in-labels) like `$(pulse)` all work. A name that is not on the list above stays visible in the status bar, so a misspelling is easy to spot.

Text in square brackets is left out as a whole when a limit named inside it is one the account does not have, which removes the separator along with the value: `✼ {5h}%[ · {opus}%]` shows `✼ 7%` without an Opus limit and `✼ 7% · 82%` with one.

The four characters `{` `}` `[` `]` are reserved and cannot appear in the text.

**Examples**

- `✼ {5h}% · {7d}%` → `✼ 7% · 3%`
- `✼ {max}%` → `✼ 95%`
- `{5h}/{7d}` → `7/3`
- `$(pulse) {5h}%[ · {fable}%]` → `$(pulse) 7% · 12%`
